title: Coinbase DCA Execution vs Plan
dataSources: Crypto prices/holdings (`crypto:price`, `wallet:balance`), exchange transactions (`coinbase:txn`), budget/transaction exports (`firefly:txn`, `ynab:txn`), bill feeds.
app: Crypto exchange/wallet APIs (Coinbase, on-chain), budgeting exports (YNAB/Firefly III), and subscription trackers via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=coinbase:txn type=buy
| bin _time span=1w
| stats count as buys, sum(usd_total) as spent by asset _time
| where buys=0 OR spent<50
| sort _time asset
description: Checks whether your dollar-cost-averaging routine actually executed on schedule and with the approximate size you expected.
value: DCA only smooths volatility if you really keep doing it; this query catches skipped weeks and undersized buys caused by cash, auth, or automation issues.
implementation: Forward exchange transaction history into Splunk; review weekly by asset and compare the actual buy count and spend to your intended cadence.
visualization: Weekly table of asset buys and total DCA spend.
grandmaExplanation: It counts when your regular automatic crypto buys did not happen or were much smaller than planned.
